frame.title: Explain why reliable decomposition needs observable seams
frame.task: Write a compact technical essay arguing when recursive agent decomposition improves reliability and when it makes results worse.
frame.product_intent: Give harness designers a useful decision model rather than a blanket recommendation to spawn more agents.

demands.statement: Distinguish throughput decomposition from reliability decomposition.
demands.rationale: Their failure surfaces and safe recursion depths differ.

demands.statement: Explain why locally green leaves can still compose into a globally broken result.
demands.rationale: This is the motivation for seam instrumentation.

demands.statement: Give an actionable stopping rule for decomposition.
demands.rationale: The reader needs a decision procedure, not only a diagnosis.

stable_context: A seam is a pre-work claim that two work regions can vary independently once their interface is fixed.
A join may be mechanical, oracle-backed, or inference-heavy.
Leaves can silently absorb interface mismatches and still return coherent local products.

referents.observed_fact: All three demands must remain visible in the finished essay.
Cross-section consistency can only be evaluated on the joined artifact.

constraints: Do not assume that deeper decomposition is automatically better.
Keep analogies to graphical models explicitly qualified as analogies.
